title: S2f2 steering_policy in shadow: deterministic triggers (dependency merged, stuck, out-of-scope, repeated gate failure, security concern) produce decision_log rows kind steering; promotion feature steering_policy (P14)
spec:
Create orchestrator/steering_policy.py. evaluate(task, *, tasks, registry_doc, stale_evidence, gate_history, cfg) -> {"action": "continue"|"steer"|"cancel", "trigger": name|None, "reasons": [...], "message": text|None}. Triggers, deterministic, in this order: security_concern (a merged sibling changed a security path the task reads: from stale_evidence stale_paths matching [review] security_paths); dependency_changed (stale_evidence risk medium or high on the task's read scope); stuck (no registry event for [steering].stuck_after_s, default 900, while status running); out_of_scope (registry tool events touching paths outside write_scope and read_scope more than [steering].out_of_scope_events, default 3); repeated_failure (two gate reds with the same failure signature on this lineage). Action: steer for dependency_changed, out_of_scope, repeated_failure; cancel for security_concern when the task is not on the critical path, else steer; continue otherwise. The message names the trigger, lists the changed paths or the repeated failure, and never restates the spec. daemon tick: for every running execute task compute evaluate and record decision_log rows kind steering (add to KINDS) with candidates continue/steer/cancel, hard constraints, deterministic evidence, selected, mode; [steering].mode = "shadow" (dated comment; off|shadow|active). Active: call worker_control.steer or cancel with the message; shadow: rows only; never more than one steering per task per [steering].min_interval_s (default 1800). promotion FEATURES entry steering_policy with criteria: at least 20 shadow rows with a steer or cancel candidate and, once active, fewer fix rounds per task than the shadow baseline with no rise in token cost. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/12-steering-policy.md.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_steering_policy.py::test_triggers_in_order_and_actions (each trigger from fixtures yields the documented action and message)

spec_review_risks.issue: Inputs are unspecified. There is no definition of how gate_history yields a 'failure signature' or how 'same lineage' is determined. Nothing says whether registry tool events carry file paths (worker_registry KINDS has 'tool', but its payload shape is not stated), or how out_of_scope compares paths against write_scope/read_scope (glob or prefix). Without that, repeated_failure and out_of_scope cannot be built or tested deterministically.

'Critical path' is undefined in the evaluate() signature. The daemon has critical_path.explain/rank, but evaluate() receives only tasks and cfg, so the policy has no durations or ranking. The cancel-vs-steer rule for security_concern is therefore unspecified, and it is a cancel of live work, so the effect is large. Also, a cancel action in active mode can kill a worker on a heuristic, so a fail-closed default is needed.

worker_control.steer requires the keyword-only 'reason' and raises ValueError when there is no live pid, thread or session. The spec does not say how the daemon tick handles those exceptions. An unguarded raise would abort the whole tick. steer also terminates and resumes the worker, which is a real interruption, so failures must be caught, logged as a row, and must not consume the min_interval_s slot.

min_interval_s state is unspecified. It must be persisted, for example by reading prior steering decision_log rows or pipeline.steer_epoch, rather than held in a module global. A global resets on daemon restart and allows a repeat steer. In shadow mode it must also be clear whether rate-limited rows still get written every tick (row flooding, and it distorts the '>=20 shadow rows' promotion criterion). Dedupe rows per (task, trigger, evidence hash).

There is no [steering] section today. Defaults must live in code (stuck_after_s 900, out_of_scope_events 3, min_interval_s 1800, mode shadow). A missing, invalid or unknown mode must fall back to off or shadow, never active. tests/test_pool.py should get a validation case, and it is not in the acceptance list.

Adding 'steering' to KINDS also needs row-shape validation. The spec lists candidates, hard constraints, evidence, selected and mode, but not the schema. The message text must be redacted or omitted from rows. tests/test_decision_log.py is not in scope or acceptance, so KINDS-related assertions (counts, allowed-kind lists) may break the base suite.

The criterion 'fewer fix rounds than baseline with no rise in token cost' needs collector support in promotion.collect(). The spec adds only a FEATURES entry, so the criterion is unmeasurable and the feature can never evaluate to promote. State whether it is deliberately manual/pending, or add the collector. Also check for existing tests that assert the exact FEATURES list or count.

The stuck trigger needs 'now' and the last registry event ts. Without an injectable clock, the deterministic test cannot run. Add a now= parameter. The security_concern trigger uses fnmatch against [review] security_paths, and an empty list must not mean 'nothing sensitive' (see the fail-closed handling in daemon.py). Say what happens then.

The shadow-mode test must assert worker_control.steer and cancel are never called, via unittest.mock. It must also cover active mode calling them once and respecting min_interval_s, and error handling. Only shadow is in acceptance, so the active-path guard is untested.
